title: OpenPLC Runtime
subtitle: IEC 61131-3 PLC runtime — C/C++ real-time core, Python REST API server, Go bootloader
advisorySource: OSV (PyPI Advisory Database, GitHub Advisory Database, Go vulnerability database) via osv-scanner
_note_ids: Every triage entry lists the advisory ids it accounts for. build-report.mjs cross-checks the live post-suppression scan against these: an advisory no entry claims is reported as untriaged.
_note_counts: advisories/counts describe the last full assessment and are only rendered when the report is built without a live scan. No assessment has been recorded yet, so they are zero.
headline: No triage has been recorded for this product yet. The numbers in the Key metrics table come from the live scan of this release; any advisory it reports is listed as untriaged until a reviewer records a VEX determination for it.
scope: The OpenPLC Runtime is deployed as a container image (or a native install via install.sh --native) holding a C/C++ real-time PLC core (plc_main, native plugins such as S7comm and EtherCAT), a Python Flask REST API server with its own virtual environment, one virtual environment per Python plugin (Modbus master/slave, OPC-UA), the EtherDOG EtherCAT master service, and a separate Go bootloader container that installs and supervises the runtime.
scopeNote: Covered: the Python packages pip resolves from requirements.txt and from every core/src/drivers/plugins/python/*/requirements.txt (each resolved on its own, as each plugin has its own venv); the Go modules of bootloader/; and the components listed by hand in security/components.json (vendored cJSON and Snap7, EtherDOG and its SOEM submodule, the CMake release install.sh installs). Not covered: Debian packages of the base image and the system CPython interpreter, and the STruC++ runtime headers that arrive with each uploaded PLC program. Vulnerability scanning covers the Python and Go parts only; the hand-maintained C/C++ components have no package-manager identity osv-scanner can match and must be reviewed manually.
methodologyNote: The requirements files are not lockfiles, so the shipped Python versions are those pip resolves at install time. The pipeline reproduces that resolution with pip install --dry-run --report and scans the pinned result, together with bootloader/go.mod, with osv-scanner against OSV, honouring the VEX baseline in osv-scanner.toml.
licenseNote: The OpenPLC Runtime is dual-licensed: GPLv3 or a commercial licence from Autonomy Logic. Third-party licences are those recorded in the SBOM. Notable: Snap7 (S7comm plugin) is LGPL-3.0-or-later, EtherDOG is GPL-3.0-or-later, and SOEM (linked into EtherDOG) is GPLv3 or a commercial licence from rt-labs.
remediation: Triage every advisory listed as untriaged and record its VEX determination.

practices.practice: SBOM generated per release in CycloneDX and SPDX
CI security gate on every pull request into development and main, blocking newly introduced critical advisories
That gate configured as a required status check
Python dependencies pinned to exact versions in the requirements files
Automated vulnerability scanning of the vendored C/C++ components
